The first eigenfunction factors into positive sine/cosine factors on the open triangle; log u is strictly concave because log sin X + log sin Y has negative-definite Hessian and each log cos of an affine argument is concave. Substituting d=-20c^5+24c^3-5c into the two cleared critical equations gives exactly the stated factors by Q(c); Q has a unique root in (93/100,47/50), the corresponding point lies in the triangle, and strict concavity makes it the unique global maximum. Independent symbolic checks reproduced both factorizations, the eliminant for d, and the quoted coordinates.
